name: Maratha Empire
summary: A Marathi state founded by Shivaji that challenged and then dominated the Mughals. It controlled much of India in the 18th century until the British defeated it in 1818.

knownFor.label: Hill and sea forts
knownFor.note: Forts like Raigad and Sindhudurg, the backbone of Maratha defence.

knownFor.label: Shivaji
knownFor.note: Founder of the Maratha state, crowned in 1674.

knownFor.label: Maratha navy
knownFor.note: A coastal fleet led by Kanhoji Angre.

location.value: The Deccan and western India, expanding into much of the subcontinent by 1760.
location.source: Wikipedia: Maratha Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Gordon, The Marathas 1600–1818 (1993)

terrain.value: The Western Ghats and Deccan plateau, with many hill forts.

climate.value: Monsoon; famines when the rains failed.

resources.value: Farmland and revenue taken from conquered regions.

disasters.value: Famines when the rains failed, such as the Doji Bara famine in the Deccan (1791–92).

urbanisation.value: Pune became the Peshwa’s seat and a major city.
urbanisation.source: Wikipedia: Maratha Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Gordon, The Marathas 1600–1818 (1993)

migration.value: Maratha chiefs and soldiers settled in conquered regions such as Gwalior, Indore and Baroda.

economicBase.value: Land revenue and the chauth (a quarter of revenue) taken from neighbouring regions.

tradeRoutes.value: Inland trade and a coastal navy under Kanhoji Angre.

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.

moneyAndTax.value: Rupee, paisa and Shivrai coins; chauth (a quarter tax).

inequality.value: Military chiefs and landholders above peasants.

governmentType.value: Absolute monarchy (to 1761), then a confederacy led by the Peshwa.

keyRulers.value: Shivaji (1674–1680), Sambhaji, Baji Rao I (Peshwa), Baji Rao II.

succession.value: The Chhatrapati was hereditary, but Peshwas came to hold real power.

institutions.value: The Ashta Pradhan (council of eight ministers).

stability.value: Fragmented into a confederacy of chiefs after 1761.

eliteConflict.value: Rivalry among the Peshwa, Scindia, Holkar, Gaekwad and Bhonsle.

armyAndTech.value: Fast light cavalry and guerrilla warfare; hill forts; a navy.

majorWars.value: Deccan Wars (1680–1707); Third Battle of Panipat (1761); Anglo-Maratha Wars.

territoryChange.value: At its height, about 2.5 million km² (around 1760), across much of India.

alliancesRivals.value: Rivals: Mughals, Durrani Afghans, Mysore, British.

inventions.value: Engineering of hill forts and sea forts such as Sindhudurg.

scienceEducation.value: Marathi literature and government records; Brahmin scholars served as administrators.

openness.value: Practical: used Persian-style revenue methods and later European officers.

religion.value: Hinduism; the Marathas also protected Muslim shrines and served alongside Muslim soldiers.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Maratha Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Gordon, The Marathas 1600–1818 (1993)

languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Maratha Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Gordon, The Marathas 1600–1818 (1993)

artsArchitecture.value: Forts such as Raigad and Sindhudurg, and temples and palaces in Pune.

socialStructure.value: Brahmin administrators, Maratha warriors, peasants and artisans.

sharedIdentity.value: The idea of “Hindavi Swarajya” (self-rule) linked to Shivaji.
sharedIdentity.source: Wikipedia: Maratha Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Gordon, The Marathas 1600–1818 (1993)

neighbours.value: The Mughals, the Durrani Empire, Mysore, the Nizam of Hyderabad and the British.

ideasReligions.value: The Marathi Bhakti saints (Tukaram, Dnyaneshwar) shaped popular religion.

colonisation.value: Annexed by the British East India Company in 1818.
colonisation.source: Wikipedia: Maratha Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Gordon, The Marathas 1600–1818 (1993)

riseSignals.value: Shivaji was crowned in 1674 after decades of guerrilla war against the Mughals and Bijapur.
riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Maratha Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Gordon, The Marathas 1600–1818 (1993)

peakPeriod.value: Controlled much of northern Indian politics, about 1737–1803, though defeated at Panipat (1761).

declineSignals.value: Defeat at the Third Battle of Panipat (1761) and rivalry between chiefs.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Maratha Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Gordon, The Marathas 1600–1818 (1993)

outcome.value: Defeated by the British East India Company in 1818.

sources.value: Marathi records. Checked against Wikipedia (“Maratha Empire”).

overallCertainty.value: Good. Well documented in Marathi, Persian and British records.
